findings.source_conclusion: Custodian absent()/identity_live() can raise EPERM into service generic catch. fail() closes grants and marks uncertainty but sets no per-record permission-denied/identity-lost terminal authority state. Later service calls retry process probes; drain can later signal if numeric identity checks succeed. findings.title: Registered-wrapper normal exit needs an observe-only terminal closure
findings.observed_evidence: Clean happy/cancel cases and completed shared-helper checks show no normal-completion termination signal. TERM/KILL signal events were retained in the three incomplete/failed acceptance cases; that does not prove the same signal occurred on a clean completion.
findings.source_conclusion: drain() can signal any inspect()-authorized record without checking released/normal-exit state. After a full completion and exit grant, a still-present numeric leader may match PID/PGID/SID, including a completed process not yet reaped. There is no observe-only gate for that state. For an already-reaped leader with absent PID, identity_live returnsFalse and inspect refuses; no claim is made that an absent reaped PID is directly signaled.
findings.required_correction: After durable completion acceptance plus matching exit grant, normal leader closure must be observe-only and sticky; no TERM/KILL solely because a saved group remains. Track any proven wrapper exit/completion as terminal and refuse re-arming. Before exit grant a protocol-held leader is a distinct state and may be retired only with still-valid live authority and no prior permission refusal. Preserve unresolved state/scratch on uncertainty. Reuse or mirror the shared VM helper policy without treating native child_reaped alone as proof the wrapper leader is reaped. Extend happy/no-ACK and selected failure controls to assert signal ordering and authority closure.
